newsitem.title: USA: Compaq cuts U.S. server prices.
newsitem.headline: Compaq cuts U.S. server prices.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp said on Wednesday that it has reduced U.S. prices up to 19 percent on select servers from its ProSignia and ProLiant product lines and up to 29 percent on select server option products.
Compaq said the price cuts, which took effect on August 19, 1996, stem from lower component costs.
The ProSignia 300 with a 90 megahertz Intel Corp Pentium processor was reduced 14 percent, to $2,799 from $3,243 for one of the lower-end servers.
In the middle of the line, the Proliant 1500T with a 166 megahertz Pentium processor was reduced by six percent, to $7,899 from $8,431, the company said.
The Prosignia 300 Model 1 with a 90 megahertz processor was reduced 19 percent, to $1,889 from $2,333, a company spokesman said. The model does not include a hard drive.
Servers with the latest Pentium Pro processors were not reduced in price, the spokesman said.
In a separate statement, Compaq said nearly 80 percent of the personal computer servers shipped with Pentium Pro processors during the 1996 second quarter were Compaq ProLiant 5000 models.
It said it was shipping the ProLiant 5000 with a board comprised of 200 megahertz Pentium Pro processors with 512 kilobytes of cache memory for $15,625.
